newsitem.title: UK: UK slowdown could boost NatWest Markets.
newsitem.headline: UK slowdown could boost NatWest Markets.

text.p: Natwest Markets, the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank Plc said on Tuesday that slower UK economic growth in 1998 would not hamper its performance and could, in fact, boost money-market income.

"We operate in 26 countries, and Britain is only one of them. Many of the businesses which we are active in would be immune to that downturn in the economy," NatWest Markets chief executive Martin Owen told Reuters in an interview.
"In effect it doesn't stop foreign exchange revenues...And it in fact could increase the volatility in the money markets. So, you could make more money," Owen told Reuters.
NatWest Bank, NatWest Market's parent company and one of Britain's largest banks, reported on Tuesday a jump in operating profits but also warned of an economic slowdown in 1998.

"Although the UK economic environment remains positive, we see the pace of growth slowing in 1998 and are adopting a more cautious approach to lending," NatWest chairman Lord Alexander said on Tuesday after announcing its results.
Owen said the warning was a "cautious overtone" to give the market an indication that it is not trying to get caught up in a heady atmosphere where nothing can go wrong.
Profit before tax was 1.12 billion pounds after exceptional items, with operating profit from continuing operations up by 339 million to 1.61 billion pounds.
NatWest shares, however, dipped after it warned of the economic slowdown and did not perform an expected share repurchase.
Pre-tax profits at NatWest Markets rose in 1996 to 462 million pounds from 304 million, although this included a fall in bad debt provision to 18 million pounds from 114 million.
"We had a very strong performance from our treasury division and have continued to see the growth of our business year-on-year," Owen said.
Owen said NatWest also saw strong growth in the corporate finance and equities division, effectively tracking those of the American investment banks.
"We have had a good year," he said.
Dealing profits at NatWest Markets grew 12 percent to 543 million stg in 1996 from 485 million in the same period last year.
Foreign exchange income, at 176 million pounds remained steady in 1996 in what the bank said were difficult market conditions.
"The principle difficulty was that they (currency markets) were not volatile and it is very difficult to make money in the foreign exchange market when it is not volatile," said Owen.

Despite the lack of volatility, however, he said NatWest Markets had been able to demonstrate the strength of its franchise and quality of its business because it continued to make money even though volatility was reduced.
"That usually means that we are increasing our volumes," he said, adding that foreign exchange volumes in 1996 were over three trillion dollars.
NatWest Markets said other dealing profits rose by 34 million pounds to 171 million, reflecting strong increases in rate-risk management products.
